Implement the RecordMatchResult use case for an amateur football league. It records the result of a scheduled match and returns the updated standings.

- The match must belong to the league and must not have a result yet.
- Goals are whole numbers, zero or more. A team can instead forfeit; a forfeit is recorded as 3–0 for the opponent.
- Win 3 points, draw 1, loss 0.
- Standings are ordered by points, then goal difference, then goals scored, then team name alphabetically.

Write a use case for enrolling a child in a kindergarten class.

Rules: the child must turn 5 on or before September 1 of the school year. A child can only have one application per school year (enrolled or waitlisted). If the class has a free seat the child is enrolled. Otherwise the child joins the waitlist: siblings of currently enrolled children are placed after the other siblings already waiting but ahead of every non-sibling; everyone else goes to the end. Return either "enrolled" or "waitlisted" with the 1-based position.

We need a use case that closes the billing period of an electricity meter when a new reading arrives.

- Readings are whole kWh. The account stores the last billed reading and its date.
- The period (days between the two reading dates) must be 27 to 33 days.
- Consumption is new reading minus last reading and cannot be negative, unless the meter was replaced during the period: then the input carries the final reading of the old meter, the new meter started at 0, and consumption = (old final − last reading) + new reading.
- Energy price per 30 days: first 100 kWh at 12 cents, next 400 kWh at 15 cents, the rest at 20 cents. The tier limits scale with the period length (limit × days / 30, rounded to whole kWh).
- Plus a service charge of 30 cents per day.
- Store the bill and move the account's last reading forward.

Write a use case for registering a product warranty from our public registration form (the JSON body is untrusted).

The form sends serialNumber, model, purchaseDate (YYYY-MM-DD) and customerId. The serial must exist in the manufacturing records and belong to the given model, and it can only be registered once. The purchase date cannot be in the future or before the unit was manufactured. Registering within 30 days of purchase gives a 24-month warranty, within 365 days a 12-month warranty; later registrations are refused. Refurbished units always get 6 months (still within the 365-day limit). Coverage starts on the purchase date.
